title.value: Implementing automation in deep brain stimulation: has the time come?
title.justification: The paper's focus is on automating deep brain stimulation using data-driven algorithms, as mentioned in the opening lines and throughout the document.
title.quote: In The Lancet Digital Health, Jan Roediger and colleagues present the results of a prospective, randomized, double-blind, crossover clinical trial assessing the therapeutic benefit of deep brain stimulation (DBS) settings derived from individual neuroimaging metrics.

extractions.description: The paper discusses the implementation of automated deep brain stimulation (DBS) using data-driven algorithms to optimize DBS parameter settings for patients with Parkinson's disease. This approach aims to maximize motor symptom control while minimizing side effects. The study evaluates the non-inferiority of this method compared to current clinical standards in a cohort of 35 patients.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily revolves around medical advancements in deep brain stimulation, focused on improving patient treatment through data-driven techniques. It doesn't directly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The work from Roediger and colleagues positions itself radically in the forecasting area, whereby most of the therapeutic decision-making around DBS parameter setting could be performed by offline simulation, thus reducing programming time and minimizing exposure to ineffective—and possibly dangerous—settings.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, focusing instead on medical and technological advancements in healthcare.
primary_category.quote: An increasing body of literature advocates for a quantitative and algorithmic transition in DBS programming. In this paradigm shift, the clinician is helped by an array of new tools (panel).

secondary_categories.justification: Given the primary focus on medical technology, there are no secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes present in this paper.
secondary_categories.quote: Many gaps will need to be filled by future studies, including how the aforementioned programming modalities will fit into clinical practice.

primary_sub_category.justification: No sub-category aligns with the focus on medical advancements in deep brain stimulation.
primary_sub_category.quote: Many other DBS indications should be investigated, especially those with long latency between DBS programming and clinical effects—eg, dystonia or depression.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes apply.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The forecasting approach to DBS programming is founded on an adaptation of the imperfect VTA model, and the algorithm was trained on a monocentric dataset.

applications.value: Automation in deep brain stimulation (DBS) programming
applications.justification: The application is explicitly detailed as the primary focus of the paper, which seeks to automate the DBS process using algorithms for enhanced efficiency in treatment.
applications.quote: The work from Roediger and colleagues positions itself radically in the forecasting area, whereby most of the therapeutic decision-making around DBS parameter setting could be performed by offline simulation, thus reducing programming time and minimizing exposure to ineffective—and possibly dangerous—settings.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper fits better under the theme of Medical Technology and Innovation due to its focus on automating medical procedures using advanced algorithms, not covered by existing climate-focused categories.
new_primary_category.quote: The pure forecasting approach of the method proposed by Roediger and colleagues should not be read as primacy for the computational model predictive approach.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Given the emphasis on developing automated solutions in deep brain stimulation, a sub-category focused on automation in medical treatments would better represent the paper's content.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Algorithm-driven online optimisation can be designed to efficiently lead the iterative programming to converge on the most performant set of DBS parameters.
